## About Us

Meridian builds scheduling software for medical clinics — the kind with four exam rooms, two providers, and one person at the front desk holding the whole day together.

We started in 2019 after spending six weeks sitting behind the counter at a family practice in Tulsa. Here is what we saw: a paper appointment book, a fax machine, and a receptionist who spent half her shift on the phone rearranging Tuesday. The software the clinic already owned could technically do scheduling. Nobody used it. Moving one appointment took eleven clicks.

So we built the thing she actually needed. Drag an appointment to a new slot and the patient gets a text. Cancel one and the waitlist fills it, usually within the hour. Providers set their own rules once (Dr. Reyes does physicals only on Thursday mornings) and the system stops offering slots that break them.

We are stubborn about a few things. Patient records stay encrypted, we sign a BAA with every clinic, and we have never sold or shared a chart. Our uptime is published on the status page, outages included. When something breaks you get a person on the phone, because a clinic that cannot see its schedule cannot see patients.

Today about 900 clinics run their day on Meridian. Most are independent practices with two to twenty providers, the ones big hospital systems keep trying to buy. We are 34 people in Denver, and a third of us came out of clinic operations.

If your front desk is still working around your software, call us.

---
